paragraphs.text: Out-of-tree patch: make @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client recover when a stateful Streamable HTTP MCP serv
er restarts, instead of failing until DSH is restarted.
# dsh-mcp-session-recovery

An out-of-tree patch that makes `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` recover when a
**stateful Streamable H

TTP MCP server stops recognising the session** underneath
a running DSH — whether because the server

restarted, or because an idle timeout
pruned the session while everything stayed up.

Without it, every tool from that server fails permanently — restarting DSH is
the only fix. With it,

the client notices the dead session and rebuilds the
connection on its own within a second or two.

> **中文摘要**：当带会话状态的 MCP 服务端（Streamable HTTP）不再认识 DSH 手里那个
> `mcp-session-id` 时（服务端重启，**或会话因空闲超时被清理**）

，该服务端的
> **所有工具调用会永久失败**，只能靠重启 DSH 恢复。本仓库是一个仓外补丁，让客户端
> 自己发现会话失效并重连，1~2 秒内自愈。
>
> ⚠️ 注意一个常见误解：**并不需要

服务端重启**。实测有服务端把会话持久化到磁盘、重启
> 完全无损，但设有 12 小时空闲超时 —— 只要 DSH 挂着超过 12 小时没有 MCP 调用，
> 同样会中招。详见下文。
>
> 上游已
知（见下方链接），官方暂不接受外部 PR，故以此形式发布。
## The bug

`dsh-mcp-client` has a complete reconnect supervisor — bounded exponential
backoff, outage-scoped at

tempt budget, tool re-sync on reconnect. It is wired to
exactly one signal:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Session loss never produces a close. The MCP SDK reports it as a **request-level
error**: the transp

ort throws `SdkHttpError` with `status: 404` and calls
`onerror` only, leaving `onclose` silent. The

dead `mcp-session-id` is retained,
because the SDK rewrites it only on a *successful handshake* — a

nd handshakes
happen only inside `connectGeneration()`, which only runs at startup or after a
reconn

andshakes
happen only inside `connectGeneration()`, which only runs at startup or after a
reconnect.
So:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Starting a new conversation does **not** help: the MCP bridge is process-scoped,
one plugin instance
per Host, shared by every session. Only a Host restart does.

A telling asymmetry: a *failed connect attempt* **does** reach the supervisor
(`settleFailedGenerati

on → generationDown → scheduleReconnect`), so a server that
is down at startup keeps being retried.

Only a session invalidated on an
**already-established** connection falls through the gap.
### What invalidates a session depends on the server

Both variants produce the same 404 and the same permanent failure, so the patch
is the same — but th

e trigger is worth knowing, because it determines how often
you hit this:
| server behaviour | trigger | notes |

| sessions held in memory | process restart | the classic case |
| **sessions persisted and restored
** | **idle timeout** | a restart is harmless; long idleness is not |

The second variant is the one verified end-to-end here. Nowledge Mem's backend
logs
[代码示例省略，未执行]

and indeed a session survives repeated server restarts (confirmed: an MCP session
created before two

consecutive app restarts still answered `200` afterwards),
while one aged past 43200s is pruned and

rejected with
`404 Not Found: Session not found`.

**Practical consequence:** leaving DSH running for more than 12 hours without an
MCP call is enough

to break the connection — no crash, no restart, nothing
visible. That is far easier to hit than a se

rver crash, and it is exactly this
shape of failure that is invisible without the patch.
## Affected versions
`lib/index.js` is byte-identical across these, so the same patch applies to both:
| version | `lib/index.js` sha256 | affected |

| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client@0.2.0-rc.2` | `758d8fc4…f5dd` | yes |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client@
0.2.1-alpha.4` | `758d8fc4…f5dd` | yes |
`grep -c onerror lib/index.js` → `0` on both.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The script finds the installed plugin, refuses to proceed if the file does not
match the revision th

e patch was cut against (unless you confirm), backs the
original up to `~/.dsh/backups/dsh-mcp-clien

t-pre-onerror-fix/`, applies the
patch in a scratch repo so a partial application cannot land, and s

yntax-checks
the result. It is idempotent.
Then restart DSH:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Verify

**Reproduce the bug and the fix offline**, with no DSH restart and no real MCP
server — a fake state
ful server invalidates its session mid-flight:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

It prints `RECOVERED` (patched) or `STUCK` (unpatched). Run it against the
[该节后续省略]
## What the patch changes
Two additions, ~35 lines, no behaviour change on any other path:

1. `isSessionLostError(error)` — a deliberately narrow predicate: `status === 404`
(which the transp

ort only produces for a request that carried a session id),
plus `400` whose body names the session

as missing/invalid/unknown/expired.
Anything else surfaces unchanged, so ordinary request errors nev

er recycle a
healthy generation.
2. `generation.onerror = (error) => { if (attemptSettled && isSessi

onLostError(error)) generationDown(generation) }`
— funnels session loss into the same disconnect pa

th `onclose` already uses.
Everything downstream (backoff, fresh handshake, tool re-sync) is the exi

sting,
unmodified machinery.
## Why this is not an upstream PR

The official repository does not accept them. From
CONTRIBUTING.md:
> We are sorry that we cannot accept external pull requests at the moment.

and the repo's PR API returns `404` — pull requests are disabled, as are issues.
The policy instead
points contributors at Discussions and at the ecosystem:

> We do not believe that packages in the official repository are inherently more
> important than pa
ckages created by the community.

So this is published as an out-of-tree patch rather than a fork. The upstream
report lives at
deepse

ek-ai/deepseek-harness#9740;
if the maintainers adopt a fix, this repository retires.
